chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Nasr ibn Mizahim al-Manqari, on the authority of Umar ibn Sa'd, on the authority of Abu Mikhnaf Lut ibn Yahya, on the authority of Abu Mansoor, on the authority of Zayd ibn Wahab, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was asked about the power of God, the Exalted, may His Majesty be glorified. He stood up as a preacher, praised God, and extolled Him.

Then he said: Indeed, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, are angels. If one of them descended to the earth, the earth would not be able to contain him due to the greatness of his creation and the abundance of his wings. And among them is one whom if the jinn and humans were tasked with describing him, they could not describe him, due to the distance between his joints and the beauty of his form's composition. How can one describe from His angels one whose distance between his shoulders and his earlobe is seven hundred years? Among them is one who blocks the horizon with one of his wings, while his body is immense. Among them is one whose belly button reaches the heavens. Among them is one whose foot is on the ground without support, in the lower air, and the earths are up to his knees. Among them is one whose nail's indentation contains all the waters, and they would fit within it. Among them is one whose eye's tear would carry ships forever, flowing for eternity. So blessed is God, the Best of Creators.

Then he (peace be upon him) was asked about the veils. He said: The veils are seven. The thickness of each veil is a journey of five hundred years, and between every two veils is a journey of five hundred years. The second veil consists of seventy veils, between every two of which is a journey of five hundred years, and its length is five hundred years. The gatekeeper of each of these veils is seventy thousand angels, the strength of each angel being equal to the strength of both jinn and humans. Among the veils are darkness, light, fire, smoke, clouds, lightning, rain, thunder, illumination, sand, mountains, dust, water, and rivers. These are varied veils, the thickness of each being a journey of seventy thousand years.

Then there are the pavilions of Majesty, which are sixty in number. In each pavilion are seventy thousand angels. Between each pavilion and the next is a journey of five hundred years. Then there is the pavilion of Glory, then the pavilion of Grandeur, then the pavilion of Magnificence, then the pavilion of Holiness, then the pavilion of Almightiness, then the pavilion of Pride, then the pavilion of White Light, then the pavilion of Unity, which is a journey of seventy thousand years by seventy thousand years. Then there is the Highest Veil.

His speech ended, and he fell silent. Umar said to him: 'I would not have survived today without seeing you in it, O Abu al-Hasan.' The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: 'These veils are not placed upon God, the Exalted, may God be exalted from that, for He cannot be described as being in a place. Rather, they are placed upon the Supreme Greatness of His creation, the size of which none can measure but Him, the Blessed and Exalted.'
ai.seo_question: What are the seven veils and the nature of God's angels according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration from Abu Mansur via Zayd ibn Wahb to illustrate the concept of *Kashf al-Hujub* (unveiling of veils), describing the colossal scale of angels and the seven layers of veils as manifestations of divine majesty rather than physical constraints. The text clarifies that these 'veils' are attributes of God's created greatness, aligning with the Shia theological principle that God is not confined by space or direction (*ghayr muqayyad bi-makan*). This description serves to awe the listener with the magnitude of creation while maintaining God's transcendence (*tanzih*).
